judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
Hi @gzeon-c4,

This report itself includes two issues in which the second issue is described by this report's paragraph that states the following:

Furthermore, the executeWithdraw function executes processedBaseTokenAmount += data.amount and totalWithdrawnAmount += processedBaseTokenAmount in which totalWithdrawnAmount and the profit calculated by the getProfit function below are positively related. Because only baseTokenAmount, which is a portion of data.amount, is actually withdrawn, increasing totalWithdrawnAmount by data.amount is too much, which causes the profit to be higher than what it should be. In this case, calling the recordProfitForFee function below would cause preformanceFeeSharesWaitingForDistribution to be higher than what it should be as well. When such preformanceFeeSharesWaitingForDistribution is minted to performanceFeeReceiver through calling the collectPerformanceFees function below, performanceFeeReceiver receives an amount of shares that is higher than what it is entitled to. Because such preformanceFeeSharesWaitingForDistribution corresponds to the profit that is higher than what it should be, the value per share is diluted and users' shares lose values incorrectly.

This second issue is exactly the same issue described by and this report and both recommend the same mitigation step. In addition, this report includes a coded POC, which is lacking

judge_and_sponsor_statements.author: d3e4
judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
@gzeon-c4 I'm not sure this is a duplicate of #1484. I understand the intention is to sometimes reduce the amount received in the withdrawal; that is not the issue here. The issue here is that the check on L560 if (balanceBefore + amount balanceAfter) revert NoyaAccountingbanalceAfterIsNotEnough(); is ineffective because it uses the wrong amount. It should not check that the amount sent is sent (this will always be the case unless it reverts; it's just a safeTransfer()), but that the requested amount is retrieved.

For reference, I did report a true duplicate of #1484 in #1347.

Hey @gzeon-c4, Thanks for the judging 

I guess the sponsor didn't get the explanation, it's mostly an architectural problem showing how their own protocol fees will have to go through the entire withdrawal phase and they'll end up charging fees on top of already locked fees which is not very good because they'll have to request a few withdrawals before the amount gets low enough to not factor in the fees over the withdrawals.

Please review it again and consider this.

 Can think of that as in a bank. When they collect taxes, those taxes are profit for them, they don't pay tax again to the bank upon withdraw.

candidate_claim.value: BalancerConnector only takes single token into account when calculating position TVL The BalancerConnector will always report a lower value for its LP position in a Balancer pool it has a position in, affecting calculation of shares/assets on deposit/withdrawals and performance fees. If a user has deposited into an AccountingManager that utilizes the BalancerConnector at a moment when the connector has a position in a pool the shares they'll get will be worth a lot more after the LP Balancer position has been decreased (or closed) as the underlying tokens will now be available in the TVL and they wouldn't have been prior to that, resulting in a larger gain for the depositor, instead of just a share of the yield accrued from the LP position.

finding.title: BalancerConnector only takes single token into account when calculating position TVL

judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt: We have a hard time comprehending how getting the weighted value of a single token from a Balancer pool can represent the entire value of the LP position? Given that the BalancerConnector allows for depositing different amounts of the tokens that the Balancer pool is composed of and that when calculating the TVL of the LP position only a single token of the pool is taken into account, there's a clear discrepancy. Any token balances that are not pool.tokenIndex will be outright ignored in the position TVL calculation. Thus, this is issue is of a valid High severity in our opinion.

candidate_claim.value: A malicious actor can affect the TVL of certain vaults causing it to drop and erasing the stored performance fee shares checkIfTVLHasDroped is a public function which can be called by anyone to burn the shares waiting for the distribution of the performance fee if the TVL has dropped, this is intentional so that everyone can prevent the strategy manager from getting "more performance fees than it should". finding.title: A malicious actor can affect the TVL of certain vaults causing it to drop and erasing the stored performance fee shares

judge_and_sponsor_statements.author: iamandreiski
judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
Hey, thanks again for your judging efforts. The issue might not be a high, but rather a medium in my opinion and a case can be made for a valid DoS. Expanding on the sponsor’s comments, I believe that the problem isn’t the public access to the checkIfTVLHasDroped() to prevent malicious managers for getting more fees than they should, but rather the way that the Curve connector TVL calculations work with its one-sided liquidity calculations. Each time that someone tries to store shares for minting, the call to the function can be sandwiched and the profit storing DoSd. The recommended fix contains and mentions that if TVL calculations on the Curve connector are performed in a different way, this attack surface wouldn't exist.

Thank you!

judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
Hi @gzeon-c4 and @HadiEsna,

thanks for going through all the issues this fast.

About this submission, respectfully, I'm afraid I have to disagree that it is invalid. 
As stated by @HadiEsna above, at the end of SNXV3Connector::mintOrBurnSUSD, "updateTokenInRegistry(collateralType)" and "updateTokenInRegistry(usdToken)" are called to update the positions for the collateral and usdToken held directly by the connector. 

The issue is that when minting sUSD, the sUSD are not send directly to the connector, only the SNXV3 internal balance of sUSD in increased. This means that "updateTokenInRegistry(usdToken)" will not account for the newly minted sUSD since they are not held by the connector. 

The exact process can be seen in the function mintUSD. The new USD are minted to the SNX protocol and the internal USD collateral of the connector account is increased.

This means, the debt of the positions held by the connector is increased but the value created by minting the new sUSD is not recorded as a new position. So in the moment sUSD is minted, the TVL of the connector is dropping by the value of the minted sUSD.
For this reason, I would argue that this issue is valid. 
Would be great if you could take a second look.

judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
Hi @gzeon-c4, I believe this issue was rightly tagged as the 183 group by the bot, albeit I agree the title of this report is a bit misleading but this issue should be considered a duplicate of #889.

I couldn't get a hold of the sponsors due to time restrictions from my end which is why I couldn't confirm which of the implementation is intended, but this bug report includes two cases:

judge_and_sponsor_statements.author: kadenzipfel
judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
1. This is falsely marked as a duplicate of From the docs: "Findings are duplicates if they share the same root cause. More specifically, if fixing the Root Cause (in a reasonable manner) would cause the finding to no longer be exploitable, then the findings are duplicates." Since the reasonable mitigation from #396 leaves this vulnerability present, this is therefore not a duplicate.
2. Similarly to the impact of this issue is that the hooks can be unexpectedly executed with the rental safe as msg.sender, which is more significant considering that the hook logic is applied to rental safe's rather than arbitrary accounts like in #396. As such, the severity of this finding should be consistent with #170.

judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
I really don't think this is a duplicate of issue #117 

The point here being that when a "BadPolicy" is deployed is not possible to remove it with kernel#executeAction/deactivatePolicy (shown as the first revert in the POC) and it stops others (of the bad actor choosing) policies to be upgraded by the kernel (In the POC I show in the second revert that now is not possible to upgrade the ECRW policy ..because BadPolicy prevents it) .

judge_and_sponsor_statements.author: alex-ppg
judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
The Warden's submission specifies that the absence of an explicit value for the deadline argument of the referenced structs will initialize their value to 0.

As evidenced by PeripheryValidation::checkDeadline in Uniswap V3 (example of ETH deployment), the transaction would fail as "expired". This means that all exact input/output swaps performed by the contract would result in failure. I believe a severity of High is appropriate and invite the Sponsor to re-visit.

candidate_claim.value: Inconsistent Behavior in Temporary Reserve Ratio Calculation After Interest Rate Changes The onSetAnnualInterestAndReserveRatioBips function in the MarketConstraintHooks contract exhibits inconsistent behavior when handling interest rate changes after the expiry of an initial temporary reserve ratio period. candidate_claim.value: Borrower can reduces APR in fixed markets causing lenders to lose funds Lenders lose funds by receiving less interest than they were supposed to get According to the documentation; borrower should not be able to reduce the APR in a fixed term market. This makes sense because in a Fixed Term market the lender does not have the opportunity to "ragequit" i.e. withdraw if they are unhappy with the rate change and as the documentation notes it leaves open a very clear rugging opportunity.

finding.title: Borrower can reduces APR in fixed markets causing lenders to lose funds

judge_and_sponsor_statements.author: laurenceday
judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
This is a valid finding, thank you - an embarrassing one for us at that, we clearly just missed this when writing the hook templates!

However, we're a bit torn internally on whether this truly classifies as a High. We've definitely specified in documentation that this is a rug pull mechanic, but there are no funds directly or indirectly at risk here, unless you classify the potential of earning less than expected when you initially deposited as falling in that bucket.

So, we're going to kick this one to the judge: does earning 10,000 on a 100,000 deposit rather than 15,000 count as funds at risk if there's no way to ragequit for the period of time where that interest should accrue? Or is this more of a medium wherein protocol functionality is impacted?

It's definitely a goof on our end, and we're appreciative that the warden caught it, so thank you. With that said, we're trying to be fair to you (the warden) while also being fair to everyone else that's found things. This is a very gentle dispute for the judge to handle: sadly the 'disagree with severity' tag isn't available to us anymore!

judge_and_sponsor_statements.author: 3docSec
judge_and_sponsor_statements.excerpt:
Hi @laurenceday thanks for adding context.

 So, we're going to kick this one to the judge: does earning 10,000 on a 100,000 deposit rather than 15,000 count as funds at risk if there's no way to ragequit for the period of time where that interest should accrue? Or is this more of a medium wherein protocol functionality is impacted?

I consider this a Med issue: because it's only future "interest" gains that are at risk, I see this more like an availability issues where the lender's funds are locked at conditions they didn't necessarily sign up for; the problem is the locking (as you said if there was a ragequit option, it would be a different story).

I admit this is a subjective framing, but at the same time, it's consistent with how severity is assessed in bug bounty programs, where missing out on future returns generally has lower severity than having present funds at risk
